event.summary: Check template changes between confinement and create resolution
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 12c79f61a627a4241707dad0cf3b55b859d2d4fc (and pending interface check at 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435). TLDR: investigating whether an environment agent could reach outside its environment when a template changes while its create request is being resolved. Source basis: confine_create reads templates separately from resolve_agent_create; the latter rereads launch_templates at 2373. At 12c79f61 the environment branch at 2394 fixes the actual host to own, and agent_launch::resolve gives templates no known recipes, so no escape established. Need inspect the later environment-launch integration at 190d844e before concluding; this interface adds a second launch route. Contract: SPEC.md Agents and environments says agents there cannot create a new environment or reach another host. Suggested bucket: highest if an authorization escape is established; currently no consequence established. Confidence: uninvestigated lead. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: yes. No execution or reproduction performed.

event.summary: Template rereads do not let confined creates escape
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 12c79f61a627a4241707dad0cf3b55b859d2d4fc; interface also checked at 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435. TLDR: considered whether a concurrent template edit could let an agent create a session outside its disposable environment. The suspected security consequence is refuted by independent routing checks. At 12c79f61, resolve_agent_create:2394–2403 always chooses own for Environment scope; agent_launch::resolve:179–184 supplies empty known_recipes/known_places. At 190d844e, create_for_agent:1997 explicitly requires scope == Fleet before the environment-launch route; resolve_agent_create:2480–2483 rejects a remaining recipe target with target.is_none(), and :2495–2504 again forces own for Environment scope. A changed installed-host template may evade the earlier template-field refusal but cannot redirect the actual launch. Contract: SPEC.md Agents and environments: 'It cannot reach another host any further than it could from anywhere else, change templates or hosts, or create a new environment.' Suggested bucket for the suspected authorization escape: highest; no escape is established. Could-be-highest: yes, original concern preserved for independent check. Confidence: confirmed source refutation. proposed_drop: source refutation by the scope == Fleet gate, target.is_none() guard, and own-host routing described above; not based on specification acceptance. possible_cover: none. No runtime execution or reproduction performed. Revises l1 from lead to candidate; no unresolved premise remains for the security consequence.

event.summary: Confined sibling deletion cannot destroy its environment
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 12c79f61a627a4241707dad0cf3b55b859d2d4fc. TLDR: checked whether lifting the deletion refusal could let an agent delete its entire sandbox or container and lose the asking session's work. Source refutes this route. resolve_scoped_target:1437–1449 restricts the target host before the delete arm proceeds; the arm at 678–686 rejects self deletion; agent_delete:2724–2735 dispatches Environment scope to sessions::delete_session_within_environment. That helper at sessions.rs:3469–3476 enters delete_session_teardown directly, and :3502–3504 calls client.delete_session_fenced. client.rs:3923–3940 sends ControlMsg::DeleteSession, with the agent-request fence flag true; no environment deletion/provider method is reached. Guard and expected connection checks remain in sessions.rs:3482–3504. Contract: SPEC.md Agents and environments: 'Deleting another session in the environment removes that session only, through the ordinary session teardown, and never the environment: the asking session is still in it, so it cannot be the environment’s last session.' Suggested bucket for the suspected whole-resource loss: highest. Could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed source refutation. proposed_drop: source route uses session-only DeleteSession and preserves guard/fence checks, rather than calling environment deletion; not specification acceptance alone. possible_cover: none. No runtime execution or reproduction performed. The fixture's host-row survival assertion was inspected as supporting test intent, not treated as observed execution.

event.summary: Check whether clone instructions falsely promise copying an environment's directory
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435. TLDR: investigating whether agents are told that cloning a disposable-environment session copies the source directory and its local changes, although the new environment should be created from recipe and repository intent. Source basis already read: the changed Clone description qualifies only its required host for ordinary sources, then says cwd/title/source launch inherit; nearby text says 'Clone takes no repository option and copies the source’s existing directory.' The new environment paragraph says clone copies the session into a new sandbox/container but does not clearly state that its disk is not copied. Contract already read: SPEC.md Agents and environments says environment Clone uses source recipe/place with launch and repository intent, 'never a copy of its disk.' Need inspect exact numbered text, the environment clone planner and initial range attribution to distinguish a false promise of content-copying from an accurate statement about path inheritance with a later exception. Suggested bucket: other (agent-facing instructions); no established destructive action or data-loss route. Could-be-highest: no established route. Confidence: lead requiring source/wording checks, no runtime behavior claimed. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: neighbour records contain no same instruction concern; prohibited coverage sources not read.

event.summary: Full instructions state the environment-clone folder exception
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435. TLDR: considered whether the agent-facing instructions promise that cloning a disposable-environment session preserves its old directory or local disk changes. The full wording supplies the new-environment exception, so no false unconditional filesystem-copy promise is established. Exact text at agent_instructions.rs:260–263: ‘A template whose target is a recipe does the same, and clone of a sandbox or container session (with no --host or --cwd) copies it into a new one. These always show the user a card, whatever the host’s settings, and a Tensorlake sandbox bills while it runs. They take no --host or --idempotency-key; the folder is the new home, or --gh clones there.’ This specifically overrides the earlier ordinary-clone cwd inheritance description at :197–201. The phrase about copying a source directory at :201 was already present at the exclusive range base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a, where ordinary Clone copied the path into launch configuration rather than copying filesystem contents; its use does not by itself promise disk replication. Attribution was checked across the full range using the path log: 12c79f61 adds confined-agent rules; 190d844e adds the environment-clone exception; no later in-range instruction changes. Source corroboration at 190d844e: agent_requests.rs:4294–4305 explicitly documents recipe/place/launch/repository rather than disk copying, and :4360–4387 builds the clone plan from repo and launch without source.cwd. Contract: SPEC.md Agents and environments says environment clone takes source recipe/place with launch and repository intent, never a copy of its disk. This is a documentation assessment based on the full instruction text, not a drop based solely on production correctness. Suggested bucket for the suspected misleading instruction: other. Could-be-highest: no established security or work-loss route. Confidence: confirmed source/wording assessment; no runtime execution. proposed_drop: the explicit later environment-clone exception specifies no --cwd and new-home placement, and the older ordinary-clone wording never specified copying filesystem contents. A clearer explicit statement about not copying disk could improve the wording, but the suspected unconditional promise is not established. possible_cover: none of the supplied neighbour records covers this instruction concern; prohibited coverage sources not read. Revises l3 from lead to candidate; no unresolved premise remains. Original suspected consequence preserved above for independent assessment.

event.summary: List counters are limited but the test also checks the exact handler refusal
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 12c79f61a627a4241707dad0cf3b55b859d2d4fc. TLDR: considered whether the new cross-host confinement tests are unable to detect wrong supervisor routing because their request counters count only lists. The counters are indeed narrower than the test commentary, but a concrete false pass for the ordinary misrouting path was not established after inspecting the full fixture and assertions. Test facts: rest_harness.rs:280–289 counts only ListSessions; run_standalone at :503–558 acknowledges connection browser setup, replies to ListSessions and ignores other RPCs. The foreign hosts in environment_fleet are standalone, while the asking environment alone has a spliced operation responder. The changed tests at agent_requests.rs:13911–13920 and :14039–14052 both await the handler and demand ErrorKind::Unauthorized with the exact ENVIRONMENT_SCOPE_REFUSAL as well as unchanged counters. A removed/misplaced confinement check that enters the ordinary awaited cross-host PromptTargetInfo path cannot silently succeed on these peers: the request receives no answer and the client returns a transport/timeout outcome rather than the asserted policy refusal. The same exact refusal oracle checks the other verb cases, while ListSessions-based work additionally trips the per-host counter. Thus this is not the undrained-cache-only assertion defect in neighbour g126/l1. The literal counter equality alone does not certify absence of arbitrary non-list or fire-and-forget traffic; the original concern about overclaiming an all-RPC boundary remains bounded here. No shipped non-list fire-and-forget operation before a later scope refusal was found in the assigned code. A deliberately reordered handler that attempted an RPC then discarded its result and returned the scope refusal might pass, but no distinct useful regression of that form was established and this is not reported as a test bug based solely on that hypothetical. Suggested bucket for the suspected test-evidence defect: other. Could-be-highest: no established user impact. Confidence: source/fixture assessment, not runtime observation. proposed_drop: combined awaited-handler and exact-refusal oracle distinguishes ordinary foreign-host dispatch from policy refusal; no source-established false-pass path remains after checking the fixture. This is a test-oracle assessment, not an assertion that production correctness alone excuses a broken test. possible_cover: none; no excluded coverage searches. Revises l4 from lead to candidate. No unresolved premise retained.
